note: One truth table for the two implementations of the alert decisions. tests/alerts.test.js reads it, and so does android/app/src/test/java/app/pulse/status/FeedReadingTest.java, which npm run build:android runs. A disagreement between the JavaScript and the Java is therefore a failed build rather than a bug report a reader has to find. This table exists because they had already disagreed: FeedReading.resolved had no counterpart in shared/alerts.js, so the phone announced recoveries and the desktop never did, through several releases, with nothing failing. Signatures here are written in the same pipe-joined form alertSignature produces; a null signature means the feed could not be read and is spelled as null, not as an empty string, because the two mean different things.

notify.why: the ordinary case: a provider that was clear is now down
the same outage on the next sweep is not a second alert
recovery is not a notify; it is the resolved table below
a component failing is worth waking someone for
components collapse to one worst-rank key, so a second degraded component is not news. This is the rule the nineteen-toast Cloudflare case exists to defend.
the same component getting worse crosses to a higher rank

CURRENT BEHAVIOUR, recorded rather than wished away: components collapse to a single worst-rank key, so improving from component:3 to component:1 presents a key the previous signature did not have and fires. Both tiers do this identically, so it is consistent rather than drift - but a reader is interrupted to be told something got better. Changing it is a product decision, not a mirror fix.
planned maintenance is not an incident
a second, different incident is its own key
a maintenance incident is dropped before the keys are compared
an unreadable feed is never an alert; unavailable is not the same as down
losing the feed during an outage must not fire again, and must not read as recovery

resolved.why: the reported issue is gone and the feed is readable
nothing was wrong, so nothing recovered. This is the row that stops a quiet-hours hold announcing the end of something the reader was never told about.
improved but not clear, so it is not a recovery
an unreachable feed is not evidence of recovery
nothing was wrong and the feed is unreadable
maintenance never produced an alert key, so its ending is not a recovery

quiet.why: inside a window that wraps midnight, before midnight
inside a wrapping window, after midnight - the case the whole feature exists for
the end hour is exclusive, so alerts resume at 07:00
the middle of the day is never quiet under a night window
one hour before the window opens
a window inside one day needs no wrap
before a same-day window, and midnight must not be treated as wrapping
the end hour is exclusive here too
equal bounds mean quiet hours are off, not a silent 24 hours - the UI cannot express always and a reader who set both the same meant to disable it
and it closes on the exclusive end
a window starting at midnight is not a wrap
and does not silently include the hour before it
